beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Adwait Changan, and this video is about turning a single finance agent into a small team of specialists. This week I built a supervisor that ranks evidence gaps by money and routes each one to the specialist who can chase it. The interesting part is what sits at the top of that queue, because no specialist in the system can close it.

props.command: Walk me through the supervisor: what it checks, how it ranks, and what it refuses to do.
output: The supervisor verifies the whole source chain before it routes anything.
Then it ranks evidence gaps by cumulative adverse impact and delegates each one.
The top-ranked gap needs a human explanation, which no specialist can produce.

beats.narration_text: The supervisor does three things, strictly in that order. It verifies the entire source chain first. Only then does it rank the outstanding evidence gaps by how much money they account for. And only then does it hand each one to a specialist. Nothing is delegated until the data underneath has been checked.

beats.narration_text: And this is the queue it produced. Revenue first, at two hundred thousand of cumulative adverse impact. Cost of goods second, at one hundred thousand. Operating expenses third, at thirty-six thousand. The ranking is not a judgement about importance. It is arithmetic over verified periods, which means a reviewer can recompute it.

beats.act: ACT 2 — THE GAP IT CANNOT CLOSE
beats.narration_text: Owner causal explanation. That is the missing evidence on the highest ranked gap in the queue, worth two hundred thousand, and it is a sentence only a human who runs the business can write. The other two want operational driver records as well, which also come from outside the system. The supervisor can rank the work. It cannot finish any of it.

beats.narration_text: Which leaves a very clear line down the middle of this system. Specialists collect and verify evidence. They do not infer causation, and they do not approve anything. The report says so in its own header, and it ends with a sentence I put there on purpose: a prioritised queue is not an approved explanation or decision.

beats.narration_text: So, the verdict. The Mycroft Finance Investigator now runs as a supervised team rather than a single agent. Before anything is delegated, a lineage specialist verifies the whole source chain. Then outstanding evidence gaps are ranked by cumulative adverse impact: revenue at two hundred thousand, cost of goods at one hundred thousand, operating expenses at thirty-six thousand, and routed across four recorded handoffs. Specialists are scoped, delegations are capped, and every result is fingerprinted. And every ranked gap is blocked on a human, because the evidence it needs is an owner's explanation that no agent in the system can write.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the prompt. Take a multi agent system I am building and tell me, for every task it delegates, what evidence would close that task and whether any agent in the system can actually produce it. Then list the tasks that are secretly waiting on a human. Run that against something you have built. The second half is where the surprises are, because a queue that looks automated is often a queue of things nobody has assigned to a person yet.

props.command: Take a multi-agent system I am building. For every task it delegates, tell me what evidence would close that task, and whether any agent in the system can actually produce it. Then list the tasks that are secretly waiting on a human.
output: A queue that looks automated is often a queue of unassigned human work.
If no agent can close a task, the honest output is an owner's name, not a summary.
